9	/-!
10	# The semilinear action descends to a localization at an invariant element
11	(campaign `G2(c)`, layer 2)
12	
13	Roadmap `AJC.picrep.etale-rep.galois`.
14	
15	## What this file is for
16	
17	`Picard/GaloisQuotientGlue.lean`'s opening audit pins the **non-affine** Galois
18	quotient as a four-layer construction with layer 1 built, and names layer 2 as
19	*quotient-localization*: for a `Γ`-stable open `U` of a semilinearly-acted `X` and
20	an **invariant** section `N`, the affine quotient localizes,
21	`(A_N)^Γ = (A^Γ)_N`.  Layer 2 is what lets layer 3's per-chart quotients be glued
22	along a stable open at all, so the `Scheme.GlueData` overlap isomorphisms have
23	something to be built from.
24	
25	This file supplies the step that layer needs first, and the one with content:
26	**the `Γ`-action itself on `A_N`**, together with its semilinearity.  Everything
27	downstream of `IsSemilinear K L S` — the invariant subalgebra, Speiser's theorem
28	`descentAlgEquiv`, and hence the affine quotient of the localized chart — then
29	applies to `A_N` by the engine already in `SemilinearAlgebras.lean`, with no new
30	descent argument.
31	
32	## Why this is at the ring level, and why the action is not free
33	
34	Two things were measured before writing, and both shaped the statements.
35	
36	*The action is not available from mathlib.*  `exact?` fails on
37	`MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (Localization.Away N)` with `N`'s invariance in
38	scope.  That failure is honest rather than an artefact of a composite goal: the
39	missing ingredient is that `γ` maps `Submonoid.powers N` **onto itself**, which is
40	*false for a general `N`* — `γ` sends `powers N` to `powers (γ • N)`.  So the
41	construction is a statement about invariant elements specifically, and
42	`powers_map_eq` is the single place `hN` is spent.
43	
44	*The ring level is the carrier the data lives on.*  A `Γ`-stable open of a
45	non-affine `X` need not be affine, so the scheme-level spelling would route the
46	reader through the section-algebra bridge before any content appeared.  The
47	content is the ring fact.  `GaloisQuotientGlue.lean` already provides the bridge
48	in the other direction (`isSemilinear_sections`: sections over a stable open carry
49	a semilinear action), so a consumer composes that with this file.
50	
51	## Contents
52	
53	* `powers_map_eq` — the denominators are preserved; the one use of invariance;
54	* `powers_map`, `powers_map_eq_forces_pow` — the invariance-free general fact, and
55	  the **non-vacuity of `hN` as a theorem**: the conclusion of `powers_map_eq`
56	  forces `γ • N` to be a power of `N`, so at any `N` where it is not, that
57	  conclusion is false;
58	* `awayAut`, `awayAut_algebraMap` — the transported automorphism and its value on
59	  the image of `A`;
60	* `awayAutHom` — the transport is multiplicative, i.e. a `Γ`-action by ring
61	  automorphisms, packaged as a `MonoidHom` into `RingAut S`;
62	* `awayAction` — that action, in the form the engine consumes;
63	* `isSemilinear_away` — **it is semilinear**, so `invariantsSubalgebra`,
64	  `descentAlgEquiv` and Speiser apply to `A_N` verbatim;
65	* `awayAut_mk'_of_invariant_num` — a fraction with invariant numerator over a
66	  power of `N` is invariant, the direction a covering argument uses.
67	
68	Stated for an arbitrary `IsLocalization.Away N S` rather than for
69	`Localization.Away N` on purpose: a consumer holding a basic open `D(N)` of a
70	chart has `Γ(X, D(N))` as its localization, not the `Localization` model, and
71	would otherwise owe a transport.
72	
73	## What this does NOT do
74	
75	It closes no `sorry` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` and witnesses **no**
76	antecedent of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` for any curve.  It does **not**
77	discharge `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient` off the affine
78	locus: layer 2's covering half (a stable open inside a chart is covered by
79	invariant basic opens, and `π_U(V)` is open), layer 3 (the `Scheme.GlueData`) and
80	layer 4 (the glued base-change iso) are all untouched, and the Hironaka trap
81	`GaloisQuotientGlue.lean` records still bites at layer 3.  Read this as one step
82	of layer 2.
83	
84	`OrbitsInAffineOpen` does not occur here and is not weakened: this file says
85	nothing about which opens exist, only what the action does on one localization.
86	
87	## Binder discipline
88	
89	`powers_map_eq`, `awayAut`, `awayAutHom` and `awayAut_mk'_of_invariant_num` need
90	**no** `K`/`L`-algebra structure on `A` and no semilinearity — they hold for any
91	`MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A`, and the section variables are `omit`ted rather
92	than carried, per the standing unused-hypothesis lesson.  Only
93	`isSemilinear_away` consumes `[Algebra L A]`, `[IsScalarTower L A S]` and
94	`[IsSemilinear K L A]`, and it does **not** consume `[Algebra K A]` or
95	`[IsScalarTower K L A]` (linter-confirmed, `omit`ted).
96	-/

104	namespace SemilinearAction
105

109	/-! ## §1. Transporting one automorphism -/
110	
111	/-- **The denominators are preserved, and this is the only use of `N`'s
112	invariance.**  The ring automorphism `γ` carries `Submonoid.powers N` onto itself.
113	
114	For a general `N` this is *false* — `γ` sends `powers N` to `powers (γ • N)` — so
115	this is exactly where `hN` is spent, and it is why everything below is about
116	invariant elements rather than about localizations in general. -/
117	theorem powers_map_eq (N : A) (hN : ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, γ • N = N) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
118	    Submonoid.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).toMonoidHom
119	      (Submonoid.powers N) = Submonoid.powers N := by
120	  ext x
121	  simp only [Submonoid.mem_map, Submonoid.mem_powers_iff]
122	  constructor
123	  · rintro ⟨y, ⟨n, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
124	    exact ⟨n, by simp [MulSemiringAction.toRingAut, hN γ]⟩
125	  · rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
126	    exact ⟨N ^ n, ⟨n, rfl⟩, by simp [MulSemiringAction.toRingAut, hN γ]⟩
127	
128	/-- **The general fact, with invariance dropped**: the image is the powers of the
129	*moved* element.
130	
131	Stated because it is what makes `powers_map_eq` a theorem about invariant elements
132	rather than a lemma that happens to carry a spare hypothesis — see
133	`powers_map_eq_forces_pow` immediately below. -/
134	theorem powers_map (N : A) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
135	    Submonoid.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).toMonoidHom
136	      (Submonoid.powers N) = Submonoid.powers (γ • N) := by
137	  ext x
138	  simp only [Submonoid.mem_map, Submonoid.mem_powers_iff]
139	  constructor
140	  · rintro ⟨y, ⟨n, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
141	    exact ⟨n, by simp [MulSemiringAction.toRingAut]⟩
142	  · rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
143	    exact ⟨N ^ n, ⟨n, rfl⟩, by simp [MulSemiringAction.toRingAut]⟩
144	
145	/-- **`powers_map_eq`'s hypothesis is not decoration, and this is the measurement.**
146	
147	A failing `exact?` on the invariance-free version of `powers_map_eq` would prove
148	only that no *one-lemma* proof exists — a much weaker fact on a composite goal.
149	So the non-vacuity is recorded as a theorem instead: the conclusion of
150	`powers_map_eq` **forces** `γ • N` to be a power of `N`. Hence for any `N` whose
151	`γ`-image is not a power of it, `powers_map_eq`'s conclusion is *false*, and every
152	construction below genuinely needs `hN` rather than merely mentioning it. -/
153	theorem powers_map_eq_forces_pow (N : A) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L)
154	    (h : Submonoid.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ).toMonoidHom
155	      (Submonoid.powers N) = Submonoid.powers N) :
156	    ∃ n : ℕ, N ^ n = γ • N := by
157	  rw [powers_map] at h
158	  have hmem : (γ • N) ∈ Submonoid.powers N := by
159	    rw [← h]; exact Submonoid.mem_powers _
160	  simpa [Submonoid.mem_powers_iff] using hmem
161	
162	variable (N : A) (hN : ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, γ • N = N)
163	variable (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization.Away N S]
164	
165	/-- The automorphism of `S = A_N` transported from `γ`, available precisely because
166	`powers_map_eq` says the denominators are preserved. -/
167	noncomputable def awayAut (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) : S ≃+* S :=
168	  IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv (M := Submonoid.powers N) (T := Submonoid.powers N)
169	    S S (MulSemiringAction.toRingAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ) (powers_map_eq K L N hN γ)
170	
171	/-- The transported automorphism computes on the image of `A`: it is `γ` followed by
172	the structure map.  This is the identity every proof below runs through, via
173	`IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`. -/
174	theorem awayAut_algebraMap (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (a : A) :
175	    awayAut K L N hN S γ (algebraMap A S a) = algebraMap A S (γ • a) :=
176	  IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_eq (S := S) (Q := S) _ a
177	
178	/-! ## §2. The transport is an action -/
179	
180	/-- **The `Γ`-action on a localization at an invariant element**, as a `MonoidHom`
181	into `RingAut S`.
182	
183	Both laws are `IsLocalization.ringHom_ext` against `awayAut_algebraMap`: two
184	automorphisms of a localization agreeing on the image of `A` are equal, and there
185	they are `one_smul` and `mul_smul` of the action on `A`. -/
186	noncomputable def awayAutHom : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* RingAut S where
187	  toFun γ := awayAut K L N hN S γ
188	  map_one' := by
189	    apply RingEquiv.toRingHom_injective
190	    apply IsLocalization.ringHom_ext (Submonoid.powers N)
191	    ext a
192	    change awayAut K L N hN S 1 (algebraMap A S a) = algebraMap A S a
193	    rw [awayAut_algebraMap, one_smul]
194	  map_mul' γ τ := by
195	    apply RingEquiv.toRingHom_injective
196	    apply IsLocalization.ringHom_ext (Submonoid.powers N)
197	    ext a
198	    change awayAut K L N hN S (γ * τ) (algebraMap A S a)
199	        = awayAut K L N hN S γ (awayAut K L N hN S τ (algebraMap A S a))
200	    rw [awayAut_algebraMap, awayAut_algebraMap, awayAut_algebraMap, mul_smul]
201	
202	/-- The induced action by ring automorphisms, in the form the
203	`SemilinearAlgebras` engine consumes.  A `def` rather than an `instance`: it
204	depends on the invariance proof `hN`, exactly as `sectionsMulSemiringAction`
205	depends on a stability proof. -/
206	noncomputable abbrev awayAction : MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) S :=
207	  MulSemiringAction.compHom S (awayAutHom K L N hN S)
208	
209	/-- **A fraction with invariant numerator over a power of `N` is invariant.**
210	
211	The direction a covering argument uses: it says the invariants of `A_N` are at
212	least as large as the localization of the invariants, i.e. the map
213	`(A^Γ)_N ⟶ (A_N)^Γ` exists.  The converse inclusion is the remaining half of
214	layer 2 and is *not* proved here. -/
215	theorem awayAut_mk'_of_invariant_num
216	    (a : A) (ha : ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, γ • a = a) (n : ℕ) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
217	    awayAut K L N hN S γ (IsLocalization.mk' S a (⟨N ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers N))
218	      = IsLocalization.mk' S a (⟨N ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers N) := by
219	  rw [awayAut, IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_mk']
220	  congr 1
221	  · exact ha γ
222	  · ext
223	    change (MulSemiringAction.toRingAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A γ) (N ^ n) = N ^ n
224	    simp [MulSemiringAction.toRingAut, hN γ]
225	
226	/-! ## §3. Semilinearity — what makes the Speiser engine apply -/
227	
228	section Semilinear
229	
230	variable [Algebra K A] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower K L A] [IsSemilinear K L A]
231	variable [Algebra L S] [IsScalarTower L A S]
232	
233	omit [Algebra K A] [IsScalarTower K L A] in
234	/-- **The action on `A_N` is semilinear over `Gal(L/K)`.**
235	
236	This is the step with downstream value: `IsSemilinear K L S` is the hypothesis of
237	`invariantsSubalgebra`, `descentAlgHom` and Speiser's `descentAlgEquiv`, so with
238	it the *whole* affine-quotient engine of `SemilinearAlgebras.lean` applies to the
239	localized chart with no new descent argument — which is what layer 3 needs at each
240	piece of a stable cover.
241	
242	One rewrite: semilinearity is checked on the image of `L`, which factors through
243	`A`, where it is `SemilinearAction.smul_algebraMap` for `A`.
244	
245	**Two binders are idle and are `omit`ted rather than carried**: neither
246	`[Algebra K A]` nor `[IsScalarTower K L A]` is consumed (linter-confirmed). The
247	proof needs only that `L` maps to `A` compatibly with the tower to `S`. -/
248	theorem isSemilinear_away :
249	    letI := awayAction K L N hN S
250	    IsSemilinear K L S := by
251	  letI := awayAction K L N hN S
252	  apply SemilinearAction.isSemilinear_of_smul_algebraMap
253	  intro γ a
254	  change awayAut K L N hN S γ (algebraMap L S a) = algebraMap L S (γ a)
255	  rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply L A S, awayAut_algebraMap,
256	    SemilinearAction.smul_algebraMap K L A, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply L A S]
257	
258	end Semilinear
259	
260	end SemilinearAction
261	
262	/-! ## §4. The payoff: the localized chart HAS a Galois quotient
263	
264	This is what layer 2 is for, and it is stated because the value of
265	`isSemilinear_away` is not visible from the statement of `isSemilinear_away`.
266	-/
267	
268	section LocalizedQuotient
269	
270	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
271	  [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
272	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower K L A]
273	  [MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A] [IsSemilinear K L A]
274	variable (N : A) (hN : ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, γ • N = N)
275	variable (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization.Away N S]
276	  [Algebra K S] [Algebra L S] [IsScalarTower K L S] [IsScalarTower L A S]
277	
278	omit [Algebra K A] [IsScalarTower K L A] in
279	/-- **A localization at an invariant element has a Galois quotient, namely `Spec` of
280	its own invariants.**
281	
282	`Spec S` with the action `awayAction` transported in §2 satisfies
283	`IsGaloisQuotient` against `Spec (S^Γ)` — all three clauses, including the
284	universal `T`-points property, for every `T`.
285	
286	**Nothing new is proved here and that is the point.** The whole content is
287	`isSemilinear_away`: once the transported action is known semilinear,
288	`isGaloisQuotient_spec` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine.lean`) applies
289	verbatim, Speiser and all. So layer 3, gluing per-chart quotients along stable
290	opens, can quote a quotient at each localized piece instead of constructing one —
291	which is the same simplification `GaloisQuotientGlue.lean`'s header records for
292	the affine case at layer 1.
293	
294	**The universe is `Type u` throughout, not `Type v`, and this is a real
295	constraint rather than tidying**: `isGaloisQuotient_spec` lives at `Scheme.{u}`,
296	so it does not apply to a `Type v` ring. §§1–3 above are universe-polymorphic in
297	`A`; only this corollary is pinned, and a consumer whose section ring sits at
298	another level owes a universe bridge here and nowhere else.
299	
300	Still **no** discharge of `HasGaloisQuotient` for a non-affine `X`: this is one
301	piece of a cover, and assembling the pieces is layer 3, where the Hironaka trap
302	bites.
303	
304	`[Algebra K A]` and `[IsScalarTower K L A]` are `omit`ted: inherited from
305	`isSemilinear_away`, consumed by neither (linter-confirmed). What the corollary
306	needs of `A` is only that it acts and maps to `S`. -/
307	theorem isGaloisQuotient_away :
308	    letI := SemilinearAction.awayAction K L N hN S
309	    letI := SemilinearAction.isSemilinear_away K L N hN S
310	    IsGaloisQuotient (specSemilinearGalAction K L S)
311	      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
312	        (algebraMap K (SemilinearAction.invariantsSubalgebra K L S)))) := by
313	  letI := SemilinearAction.awayAction K L N hN S
314	  letI := SemilinearAction.isSemilinear_away K L N hN S
315	  exact isGaloisQuotient_spec K L S
316	
317	end LocalizedQuotient
318	
319	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

56	
57	* it predicted the converse would need "no finiteness" — correct — but also that it was a

variable (G A B K L : Type*) [Group G] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [MulSemiringAction G B]
  [Algebra A B] [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A K] [Algebra B L] [Algebra A L]

on the fraction field `L` of `B`. -/

instance smulDistribClass [SMulCommClass G A B] :

    SMulDistribClass G B L :=

    rw [Algebra.smul_def', Algebra.smul_def', smul_mul']
    congr
    apply fieldEquivOfAlgEquiv_algebraMap⟩

# Galois quotient gluing, layer 1: the section-level semilinear action (campaign `G2(c)`)

Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(L/K)` and let `X` be a
scheme over `Spec L` with a semilinear `Γ`-action `ρ` (`SemilinearGalAction`).  This
file opens the discharge of the last `G2` gate, `HasGaloisQuotient` (the gluing step
`G2(c)`), with the **overlap audit** (recorded below, before any Lean) and the first
construction layer.  **Update 2026-07-30:** layer 1 turned out to close the gate
outright for an **affine** `X` — `Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean` uses the
`U = ⊤` instance of the section action below, plus transport along `X.isoSpec`, to get
`hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine` as a global instance.  So the layers below are now
needed only for the **non-affine** case (the campaign's glued `J'_r`), and layer 3 may
quote a per-chart quotient instead of constructing one.  The first
construction layer: on every `Γ`-stable open `U` the action transports sections,
making `Γ(X, U)` an `L`-algebra with a semilinear `Γ`-action by ring automorphisms —
the section-level face of `SemilinearGalAction`, i.e. exactly the input format of the
affine quotient theorem `isGaloisQuotient_spec` — together with the scheme-level
restriction `ρ.restrict hU` of the action to `U` and the Spec-functoriality bridge
identifying the restricted action on an affine stable `U` with the `toSpecAut` action
of the section action under `hUa.isoSpec`.

## MANDATORY OPENING AUDIT (milestone 0 — recorded before proving; the overlap pin)

The glue construction needs the overlaps `U ⊓ V` of the stable affine cover to be
manageable.  `U ⊓ V` is always `Γ`-stable and open, but **need not be affine** when
`X` is not separated.  Verdicts on the two pinned resolutions:

* **(a) Stable affine *basic*-open refinement with affine pairwise intersections: NOT
  extractable in general.**  Counterexample genus: the doubled affine plane
